blocks.text: Managing Zoom meetings as a patient care coordinator

Your role as a coordinator means you are the bridge between patients and clinical teams. You likely have multiple Zoom meetings daily for care team syncs or patient check-ins. On a Mac, the Zoom desktop client is your primary tool. It integrates well with macOS but requires specific settings to stay secure and efficient.

Start by organizing your workspace. Use Stage Manager or Mission Control to keep your EHR tab separate from your Zoom call. Never share your entire screen if you have sensitive patient records open. Use the Share Screen option to select only the specific application window you need to show.
Essential Zoom keyboard shortcuts for Mac

items: ⌘ ⇧ A: Mute or unmute your audio.
⌘ ⇧ V: Start or stop your video.
⌘ ⇧ H: Show or hide the meeting chat.

blocks.text: Memorizing these shortcuts saves you from searching for buttons while a patient or doctor is waiting. If you need to check your current shortcuts, open Zoom, go to Settings, and select Keyboard Shortcuts. You can customize these to match your muscle memory.
Fixing common Zoom issues on macOS

If your camera is not working, check your macOS System Settings first. Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Camera. Ensure Zoom is toggled on. The same applies to your microphone in the Privacy & Security > Microphone section. If you still have trouble, try restarting the Zoom app.
If you see a black screen when sharing, it is often a permissions issue. Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Screen Recording and ensure Zoom is enabled in the list.

blocks.text: Using Lazur to manage your day

Lazur helps you stay in the flow. Instead of clicking through menus, hold ⌥ ⌘ and ask Lazur where a setting is. It will circle the button for you. If you need to draft a follow-up email after a meeting, hold fn and dictate your notes directly into your email client or EHR.

items: Use a dedicated headset to improve audio quality for patient calls.
Use a virtual background to maintain a professional appearance if you work from home.
Keep your Zoom app updated to the latest version to ensure security patches are applied.
Disable meeting notifications during patient calls to avoid distractions.
Use the waiting room feature to control who enters your meeting, ensuring HIPAA-compliant entry for patients.

blocks.text: Consistency is key. If you handle many patient appointments, create a standardized meeting template. This includes your waiting room settings and recording preferences. You can save these as defaults in the Zoom web portal settings.
Handling patient data during Zoom calls

Privacy is your top priority. Always double-check your screen share settings before showing a patient record. If you are recording a session for documentation, ensure you have the necessary consent. Store your recordings in a secure, encrypted location rather than leaving them on your desktop.

If you use a Mac, use FileVault to encrypt your entire drive. This adds a layer of protection to any local files you might accidentally save during a call. Regularly clear your Zoom cache if you find the app becoming sluggish after long days of back-to-back meetings.

faq.question: Can I use Zoom on an older Intel-based Mac?
faq.answer: Yes, but performance may vary. For the best experience, use an Apple Silicon Mac. Keep your macOS updated to the latest version.

faq.question: How do I ensure my Zoom meetings are HIPAA compliant?
faq.answer: Use the waiting room feature, require a passcode for all meetings, and ensure you are using a secure, private internet connection.

faq.question: Does Lazur record my Zoom meetings?
faq.answer: No. Lazur only sees your screen when you hold the shortcut key to ask a question. It does not store your audio or video.
